agenda.item: Planned VdC field study on smoking behavior.
agenda.details: Continuation of the discussion. Dr. Adlkofer explained the scientific background and goal of the planned study. He thinks that it is incorrect to talk about the planned study as a compensation study, since a nicotine uptake regulation can only be measured by a corresponding change of the nicotine offer. Rather, we are dealing here with a comprehensive study of smoking behavior, which may allow certain conclusions on a possible compensation. Past studies and more recent studies cited in the press on the problem of compensation are short-time studies conducted with a relatively small number of smokers and therefore do not correspond to the market situation. Moreover, the cigarettes used in these studies differ from the commercial cigarettes not only in the amount of nicotine, but also in other smoke components. Even so, the numerous studies talk about the presence of a compensation. The problem of compensation has by no means been clarified. While the planned study can’t supply a definite answer to the compensation problem, it may produce new information about nicotine uptake in relation to cigarette brand and smoker type.
